When I first started on Reddit, I was depressed, fascinated by this website that seemed like an exclusive club- full of awesome people and news and stuff that no-one else would be able to access because they didn't know that the Narwhal baconed at midnight. I spent 2 years on the site, contributing lightly, and not making a huge impact on the community.

Once I started pulling out of my depressive state, I started realising what the site actually was: A finely built conglomerate of power-users manipulating the flow of articles into a self-repeating circle-jerk of epic proportions.

Most people left the site due to the "safe spaces" and "SJW" bullshit, but my real motivation for leaving was the massive culture surrounding getting posts on the front page, karma and re-posting (a la gallowboob).

I'm in a much better place now, and a lot happier. I feel more included in this community, and that's what we are: A community, not an exclusive club. I've seen the subverse I moderate (sameless plug for /v/guildwars2 ) grow from 11 subs when I took over to 28 (as of 26/05/15), and I couldn't be more excited. I feel like a real member of this community, and I really look forward for a couple good years of this.

Voat is growing to be a true "safe space"- one where free speech is protected, and hopefully one where people are respected, and not endlessly censored for unpopular opinions. Everyone has a right to what they want to say, it's your responsibility to ignore those who are intentionally trying to infuriate you.

I truly believe that all people are capable of good, civility and compassion, and I hope that it will shine through here as we strive to integrate newcomers into our community, as well as work on reforming those who wish to be here, but can't or won't contribute in a positive way. Voat has so much potential right now, let us keep on going this direction, and make Voat one of the greatest internet communities ever. When my great-grandchildren are studying 21st century internet, I want Voat to be there as a prime example of a link-aggregate and global community site.
